This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act SCCH 15 3 MVC No.4268/2023 seeking Compensation of 3,00,000/ for the injuries sustained in a Road Traffic accident.

sentences.text:
2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 02.07.2020 at about 3.00 a.m., when the Petitioner was proceeding to his mother's sister's house as a pedestrian and reached KSFC Layout, near Lingarajapura, Bengaluru, at that time, one Auto bearing Reg.No.KA03D8146 driven by its driver came in a rash and negligent manner and with great speed and dashed against the Petitioner and ran on the right side of the leg of the Petitioner and caused accident and left the spot.
Due to the said accident, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was taken to Zion Hospital,
Kammahalli, wherein he admitted as an inpatient.

The Petitioner had spent huge amount towards SCCH 15 4 MVC No.4268/2023 medical expenses, conveyance,
nourishment and other incidental charges etc.,
Prior to the date of the accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was a Student.
The accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the Auto bearing Reg.No.KA03D8146 by its driver.
The Respondent No.1 is the driver and the Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending Auto bearing Reg.No.KA03D8146.
Therefore, both Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
3. In pursuance of service of Notice to the Respondent No.1 and 2, they remained absent and they were placed exparte.
4. Heard.
Perused the Petition and the materials available on record.
Now the point arises for the determination of this Court are as under : SCCH 15 5 MVC No.4268/2023 Points 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 02.07.2020 at about 3.00 p.m., at KSFC Layout, near Lingarajapura, Bengaluru,
due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Auto bearing Reg.No.KA03D 8146?

2 2.
Whether the Petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for?

If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay ?

5. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 9 documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.9 and closed his side evidence.
Since, the Respondents were placed exparte, there is no Respondents evidence.

Having heard the arguments and upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Points are as under:
 Point No.1 : In the Affirmative.
 Point No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Point No.3 : As per the Final Order,
 for the following :
 REASONS 7.

Point No.1: It is the case of the Petitioner that, he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Auto bearing Reg.No.KA03D8146 by its driver.
8.
In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, he got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 9 documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.9 and he has reiterated the Petition averments in his Chiefaffidavit.
Ex.P.1 to 9 are the FIR, Complaint, Charge SCCH 15 7 MVC No.4268/2023 sheet, Spot mahazar and Spot Sketch, Police Notice with Reply, IMV report, Wound certificate, Lab report and Medical bills.

9. Upon going through the documents exhibited, Ex.P.1 and 2 are the True copies of the FIR and Complaint which shows that on the Complaint lodged by one Manjula W/o Nanjundappa, the Banaswadi Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the offending Auto bearing Reg.No.KA 03D8146 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279 and 337 of IPC.

Ex.P3 is the Certified copy of the Charge sheet which shows that after thorough investigation, the PSI of Banaswadi Traffic Police Station has submitted Chargesheet against the driver of the offending auto for the offences punishable under Sec. 279 and 338 of IPC and under Sec.134(A&B), 187, 146 and under Sec.196 of IMV Act.
Ex.P4 is the Spot mahazar with Spot Sketch which shows that the concerned police had drawn mahazar and sketch at the spot in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P5 is the Police Notice with Reply.
ExP6 is the IMV report SCCH 15 8 MVC No.4268/2023 which shows that the said accident does not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the offending vehicle.
Ex.P.7 is the Wound certificate of the Petitioner which shows that the Petitioner had sustained grievous injury.
Ex.P8 is the Lab reports and Ex.P9 is the Medical bills of the Petitioner.

sentences.text: The ChargeSheet is the material document which clearly shows that the I.O. has Charge sheeted the driver of the offending Auto for the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and the accident caused by him and due to the said accident, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injury.
It is pertinent to note here that in spite of service of notice to the driver and owner of the offending vehicle i.e., Respondent No.1 and 2, they remained absent.
Therefore, there is no rebuttal evidence.
Further, the contents of Exhibits remained un controverted.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and oral and documentary evidence, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the Petitioner has proved the said accident has SCCH 15 9 MVC No.4268/2023 been caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and in the said accident, he had sustained grievous injuries.

Accordingly, I answer Point No.1 is in the "Affirmative".
11. Point No.2:
As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred by the rash and negligent riding of the driver of the offending Auto, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
12. It is stated in the petition that, the Petitioner is aged 16 years at the time of accident.
It is established that the Petitioner had suffered from injury in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending auto.
The Petitioner has contended that he had sustained grievous injury and he has spent huge amount for his medical treatment and other incidental charges.

The Petitioner has produced Wound Certificate at Ex.P7 issued by the Zion SCCH 15 10 MVC No.4268/2023 Hospital, wherein it clearly mentioned that the Petitioner had sustained fracture of both bones of right leg.
The Doctor has opined that the said injury is grievous in nature.
13. The Petitioner did not choose to examine the doctor who has issued the Wound Certificate as per Ex.P7.
The Petitioner has produced the Medical bills to prove expenditure towards medicines.
The bills at Ex.P9 would reveal that the Petitioner spent Rs.66,132/ towards medicines.
Apart from this, the Petitioner has not produced any documents to show that, he spent huge amount towards treatment as contended in the petition.
14. The Petitioner has not produced Physical Disability Certificate.

Hence, considering the gravity of the injuries, pain and suffering, Medical expenses, food and nourishment and conveyance, it would be lawful to award global compensation of Rs.1,00,000/ to the Petitioner.

Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending Auto bearing Reg.No.KA03D8146.
In this case, the Respondent No.1 is the driver and Respondent No.2 is the RC owner of the offending vehicle.
The Chargesheet clearly exhibits that the offending vehicle does not had policy at the time of accident.
Therefore, the Respondents are liable to satisfy the award amount.

The Respondent No.2 being the RC owner has Nandakumar vs Robert.A on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139346641/
4 to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.

sentences.text: Accordingly, I answer Point No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
16. Point No.3:

In view of my findings on Points No. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents U/S 166 SCCH 15 12 MVC No.4268/2023 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for Global Compensation of Rs.1,00,000/ along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the owner of the Offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

On deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, since the amount is meager, the entire amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of Epayment after his proper identification.

The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
SCCH 15 13 MVC No.4268/2023 Draw Award accordingly.
